operational_hypothesis: A network improves iteration and sample efficiency when a node is represented as a stateful local submodel rather than a scalar operator, and a bounded controller learns when to instantiate, route, merge, or retire such submodels under a fixed parameter and compute budget.

evidence_ledger.title: Dendro-plexing of Single Input Spikes via Multiple Synaptic Contacts Can Enhance Cortical Neuron Computation and Reduce Axonal Wiring
evidence_ledger.authors: Beniaguev D, Shapira S, Segev I, London M
evidence_ledger.verified_claim: A filter-and-fire model with multiple synaptic contacts and dendritic filtering has threefold higher memory capacity than a leaky integrate-and-fire model on a precise spike-timing task and recognizes spatiotemporal MNIST patterns where the integrate-and-fire model fails.
evidence_ledger.engineering_implication: Single nodes may need temporal state and multi-timescale local computation.
evidence_ledger.scope_limit: This is a specific model and task result, not evidence that every biological neuron equals an arbitrary model.

evidence_ledger.title: Multi-output computation by single neuron biophysics in a visual system
evidence_ledger.verified_claim: Biophysical analysis finds evidence that some fly visual interneurons may be multi-output devices; within a linear approximation a neuron is equivalent to a hierarchy of virtual neurons pooling over multiple spatial scales.
evidence_ledger.engineering_implication: A local node may expose multiple outputs or internally instantiate a hierarchy.
evidence_ledger.scope_limit: Preprint and model-dependent equivalence; not a universal equivalence between one neuron and one task model.

evidence_ledger.title: Implementing feature binding through dendritic networks of a single neuron
evidence_ledger.authors: Tang Y, Jia S, Huang T, Yu Z, Liu JK
evidence_ledger.verified_claim: Dendritic branches with strong sublinearity can act as computational units through which a single Purkinje-cell model addresses feature binding.
evidence_ledger.engineering_implication: Local nonlinear gating across branches can implement capabilities traditionally assigned to a network layer.
evidence_ledger.scope_limit: Task-specific modeling result; it does not imply general language-model capacity.

evidence_ledger.title: Single organic electrochemical neuron capable of anticoincidence detection
evidence_ledger.authors: Harikesh PC, Gao D, Wu HY, Yang CY, Tu D, Fabiano S
evidence_ledger.verified_claim: A dendritic organic electrochemical neuron performs XOR classification within a single neuron and supports edge detection in a tactile sensing system.
evidence_ledger.engineering_implication: A node with dendritic state can implement a linearly non-separable local computation.
evidence_ledger.scope_limit: A specialized physical neuron and task; not a general model.

evidence_ledger.title: Distribution and voltage dependence of ion channels shape single-neuron computations
evidence_ledger.authors: Vieira RM, Deistler M, Guillemet C, Schilling T, Macke JH, Borst A, Groschner LN
evidence_ledger.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
evidence_ledger.verified_claim: Subcellular ion-channel localization and properties shape single-neuron computation and are required in a biophysically constrained model to reproduce directional tuning.
evidence_ledger.engineering_implication: Useful node abstraction may depend on where computation occurs inside the node.
evidence_ledger.scope_limit: Supports spatially structured local computation, not model-level generality.

rejected_interpretations: Every biological neuron is equivalent to an LLM.
A single neuron universally contains the same capability as an arbitrary trained model.
A biological analogy alone proves learned module birth will improve coding ability.
Unbounded growth is acceptable without parameter, compute, or dead-module costs.
provisional_claim: The defensible 2025-2026 finding is that single neurons can carry substantially richer local computation than a scalar point-neuron abstraction. It motivates, but does not establish, learned submodel growth in an artificial network.

neuron_module.initialization: zero-gated residual child attached to a declared parent
forbidden_shortcuts: counting a scalar MLP neuron as a newly born model without independent local state
adding parameters without counting them in the 20:1 corpus budget
allowing birth only on benchmark-specific identifiers
continued growth after the final network is frozen

expert_factory.definition: The model must synthesize a new expert from its current computational state rather than only choose among a fixed expert pool.
expert_factory.minimal_generation_method: A context-conditioned hypernetwork generates low-rank residual-expert weights; topology selection may be added only after weight synthesis is validated.
counts_as_generated_expert_only_if: weights depend on the current parent and residual context
two different contexts produce measurably different expert parameters
the expert is not selected from a fixed pretrained pool
the expert cannot be replaced by a constant clone without losing the measured gain
the expert and factory parameters count toward the parameter budget
the expert is zero-gated at birth
does_not_count: choosing one fixed expert with a router
activating an unused parameter block with no generated weights
cloning the parent expert without context-conditioned synthesis
adding a scalar gate or scalar MLP and calling it an expert
generating an expert with validation or test outcomes

expert_synthesis_ladder.name: fixed-pool routing
expert_synthesis_ladder.description: Select among predefined experts; MoE reference only.

expert_synthesis_ladder.name: generated fixed-shape weights
expert_synthesis_ladder.description: Context-conditioned hypernetwork generates low-rank residual weights for a fixed expert shape.

expert_synthesis_ladder.name: generated capacity and routing
expert_synthesis_ladder.description: Factory generates rank/width, input/output routing, gate, and weights from the current residual state.

expert_synthesis_ladder.name: generated typed micro-architecture
expert_synthesis_ladder.description: Factory selects and connects a constrained typed operation graph with generated weights.

moe_boundary.disentanglement_requirement: G4 must beat G5 at matched final parameters and inference compute, and generated experts must be non-constant across contexts.
reject_if: G4 behaves as a soft router over a fixed pool
G4 experts collapse to one pattern
G4 gains disappear after removing extra inference compute or parameter headroom

episode: decide whether to synthesize an expert
adapt for a bounded number of steps
compare task gain and resource cost
commit, merge, or retire the expert
meta_growth_learning.objective: expected task improvement minus parameter, compute, birth, and dead-module costs
meta_growth_learning.controller_target: A birth is useful only when its post-adaptation gain exceeds random-expert and fixed-MoE expectations.
meta_growth_learning.meta_train_validation_split: Disjoint training tasks; meta-validation is never used to generate experts.
meta_growth_learning.final_training_phase: Freeze the factory and the final expert set before primary evaluation.

growth_controller.when_growth_is_allowed: training only, after warmup and before the final frozen phase

budget.primary_compute_budget: no more than 1.1x static matched control
budget.absolute_growth_mode: forbidden for the primary claim; diagnostic only and never a headline
capacity_reallocation: reject the birth if no headroom can be recovered

ablation_arms.name: fixed control
ablation_arms.description: No growth; same shared decoder and parameter tier.

ablation_arms.name: static width/depth
ablation_arms.description: Use the generation budget to widen or deepen the decoder without learned births.

ablation_arms.name: random births
ablation_arms.description: Birth the same number and size of modules at fixed random times.

ablation_arms.name: error-triggered births
ablation_arms.description: Birth from residual error or dead-capacity signals without a learned controller.

ablation_arms.name: learned neurogenesis
ablation_arms.description: A learned controller implements at least S2: it synthesizes context-conditioned weights, capacity, and routing, then learns bounded birth, merge, and retirement decisions.

ablation_arms.name: matched MoE
ablation_arms.description: A fixed expert pool with parameter- and compute-matched routing, but no generated expert.

promotion_gates: A child module is zero-gated and numerically inert at birth.
Generated expert weights, capacity, and routing change materially with parent/error context and are not a constant clone.
Net trainable parameters do not increase beyond the declared matched tier.
Every born module has nonzero gradient or an explicit dead-module diagnosis.
Learned growth beats random births, static width/depth, and the fixed-expert MoE at matched final parameters and inference compute.
At least one coding or engineering task improves by five percentage points with paired evidence.
Language-retention regression is at most one percent relative.
Final unique parameters remain at or below 23M for the primary claim and within the 20:1 budget.
Final inference contains no dynamic births or evaluator calls.
The effect persists across two seeds before any larger confirmation.
evidence_boundary: Neuroscience motivates a local-state and module-growth hypothesis. No experiment in this repository yet establishes that learned neuron/model birth improves coding or engineering ability.
